note: Literature reports for FILIP1-related disorder frequently describe facial hypotonia and congenital contractures/arthrogryposis co-occurring.

evidence.text: Schnabel et al. describe patients with homozygous FILIP1 variants presenting with muscular hypotonia, facial hypotonia, scoliosis, and congenital contractures affecting multiple joints.

source.title: Homozygous loss-of-function variants in FILIP1 cause autosomal recessive arthrogryposis multiplex congenita with microcephaly
source.quote: Here, we report five affected individuals from three independent families sharing an overlapping phenotype with congenital contractures affecting shoulder, elbow, hand, hip, knee and foot as well as scoliosis, reduced palmar and plantar skin folds, microcephaly and facial dysmorphism.

evidence.text: Watts et al. report a FILIP1-associated case exhibiting flexion contractures, scoliosis, facial hypotonia, and high arched palate.

source.title: FILIP1-associated neuromuscular disorder and phenotypic blending due to paternal UPD6
source.quote: Additional clinical features included flexion contractures, scoliosis, facial hypotonia and high arched palate.
